description: How is Postgres running? RED for txn_agg, then statements, connections and locks, rows and I/O, tables and vacuum, storage. From postgres_exporter: Postgres's own statistics, never table data.

panels.title: Transactions/s
panels.description: Rate. Committed plus rolled-back transactions per second in txn_agg, over the last minute.

panels.title: Rollback ratio
panels.description: Errors. Share of transactions rolled back over the last 5 minutes: a failed consumer batch (then retried one by one), a statement timeout, or an API error. 1% is a starting line, not an SLO.

panels.title: Deadlocks
panels.description: Errors. Deadlocks Postgres detected in txn_agg over the selected range. Postgres cancels one side; any value is worth a look at the statements involved (Postgres logs them).

targets.expr: sum(((sum by (datname) (pg_stat_database_deadlocks{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (datname) (pg_stat_database_deadlocks{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (datname) (pg_stat_database_deadlocks{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (datname) (min_over_time(pg_stat_database_deadlocks{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range]))))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Statement mean
panels.description: Duration. Statement time divided by calls over the last 5 minutes, every role. A route's latency is the sum of its statements plus pool wait. From pg_stat_statements (the 50 statements with the most time).

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Client connections to txn_agg, any state. Orange above the budget of 29 (4 consumers × 3, API 10, Grafana 5, exporter 2); red near max_connections (100).

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of block reads served from shared buffers over the last 5 minutes. Below 99% the working set no longer fits in memory and reads go to disk.

panels.title: Oldest open tx
panels.description: Age of the longest-running open transaction in txn_agg. A long one holds locks and stops autovacuum from cleaning dead rows. Orange from 1 minute, red from 5.

panels.title: Postgres up
panels.description: Whether the exporter could connect to Postgres on its last scrape. No data means the exporter itself is down, not necessarily Postgres.

panels.title: Rate: transactions/s
panels.description: Committed plus rolled-back transactions per second in txn_agg.

panels.title: Errors: rollbacks/s and deadlocks/s
panels.description: Transactions rolled back, and deadlocks detected, per second. A flat zero is healthy.

panels.title: Duration: mean statement time by role
panels.description: Statement time divided by calls per role. The consumers' batch insert writes up to 100 rows per statement, so it is slower per call than an API read.

panels.title: Max DB transactions/s
panels.description: The most database transactions committed or rolled back in one second, between consecutive scrapes. A consumer batch of up to 100 rows is one transaction, so this is far below the Consumers dashboard's transactions/s. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max DB transactions/min
panels.description: The most database transactions in any 60 seconds of the selected range. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max rows inserted/s
panels.description: The most rows Postgres inserted in one second. Rows skipped by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING are not inserts. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max busy connections
panels.description: The most connections executing statements at once, averaged over 10 s (statement time per second). Near the pool sizes (consumers 3 each, API 10) the pools, not Postgres, are the limit. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max connections
panels.description: The most client connections open to txn_agg. Orange above the budget of 29. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: Max statement mean
panels.description: The slowest minute of the range for the average statement. Rising with load means Postgres is the bottleneck; flat while throughput stops climbing means the limit is elsewhere. The highest value observed in the selected time range, so it stays after the traffic stops.

panels.title: DB transactions/s (10 s resolution)
panels.description: Database transactions per second between consecutive scrapes.

panels.title: Rows inserted/s (10 s resolution)
panels.description: Rows Postgres inserted per second between consecutive scrapes. Should match the Consumers dashboard's rows inserted.

panels.title: Statements/s by role
panels.description: Statements executed per second, per login role.

panels.title: Busy connections by role
panels.description: Statement time per second: the average number of connections busy executing at once (Little's law, the same sizing as the pool budget). The dashed line is every statement in txn_agg, from pg_stat_database; the roles count the 50 statements with the most time.

panels.title: Slowest statements
panels.description: Statements in txn_agg that ran in the selected range, slowest mean first. Mean, total and rows count only the range. Share is this statement's part of all statement time in the range: the place to look when the database is busy. From pg_stat_statements: the 50 statements with the most total time, the exporter's own excluded. Click a statement to see its full text (cut at 200 characters).

targets.expr: (((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))) / (((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))) > 0)) * on (queryid) group_left (query) pg_stat_statements_query_id

(((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))) > 0) * on (queryid) group_left (query) pg_stat_statements_query_id

(((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))) and on (queryid, user) (((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))) > 0)) * on (queryid) group_left (query) pg_stat_statements_query_id

(((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_rows_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_rows_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_rows_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_rows_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))) / (((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))) > 0)) * on (queryid) group_left (query) pg_stat_statements_query_id

(((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))) / scalar(sum(((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_seconds_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))))) and on (queryid, user) (((sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (queryid, user) (pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (queryid, user) (min_over_time(pg_stat_statements_calls_total{datname="txn_agg"}[$__range])))) > 0)) * on (queryid) group_left (query) pg_stat_statements_query_id

panels.title: Connections by role
panels.description: Client connections to txn_agg per login role, stacked. Dashed line: the budget of 29. Each role carries its own CONNECTION LIMIT.

panels.title: Connections by state
panels.description: Idle is normal: pools keep connections open. Idle in transaction means a client opened a transaction and stopped talking, holding its locks.

panels.title: Locks by mode
panels.description: Locks held or awaited in txn_agg. AccessShare is every read; a rise in RowExclusive is writes; anything Exclusive blocks readers.

panels.title: Oldest transaction by role
panels.description: Age of each role's longest-running open transaction. Red line at 5 minutes.

panels.title: Rows written/s
panels.description: Rows inserted, updated and deleted per second, as Postgres counts them. Inserts should track the Ingest dashboard's rows inserted/s.

panels.title: Rows read/s
panels.description: Returned: rows read by scans. Fetched: rows fetched through indexes. Returned far above fetched means sequential scans read rows they then throw away.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of block reads served from shared buffers. Dashed line at 99%.

panels.title: Temp files written/s
panels.description: Bytes queries spilled to temporary files because a sort or hash did not fit in work_mem. Zero is normal here.

panels.title: Sequential scans/s (top 10 tables)
panels.description: Full scans per second per table. On a small lookup table (categories) they are cheap and expected; on a transactions partition they mean a query missed its index.

panels.title: Dead rows (top 10 tables)
panels.description: Row versions left by updates and deletes, waiting for autovacuum. The transactions table is insert-only, so dead rows there come from rolled-back batches.

panels.title: Tables
panels.description: Every table in txn_agg, largest first; the transactions partitions are transactions_pYYYYMMDD. Table usage, at the bottom, sums them per table. Scans count the selected range. Seq scans on a large partition from the API mean a query is not using an index. Dead % above 20% that does not come down means autovacuum is falling behind. An empty Since autovacuum means it has never needed to run.

targets.expr: sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"}) / ((sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_live_tup{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"}) + sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_n_dead_tup{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"})) > 0)

((sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (relname) (min_over_time(pg_stat_user_tables_seq_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"}[$__range]))))

((sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"} offset $__range)) >= 0 or (sum by (relname) (pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"}) - sum by (relname) (min_over_time(pg_stat_user_tables_idx_scan{datname="txn_agg", schemaname="txn_agg"}[$__range]))))

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: txn_agg on disk: tables, indexes and TOAST. pg_partman drops partitions older than 18 months, so it should level off.

panels.title: WAL size
panels.description: Write-ahead log segments on disk. Grows with write bursts and shrinks after checkpoints.

panels.title: Checkpoints/min
panels.description: Timed: on schedule (checkpoint_timeout). Requested: forced because WAL reached max_wal_size. Frequent requested checkpoints mean writes outpace the WAL size.

panels.title: Exporter scrape duration
panels.description: How long the exporter's queries take each scrape. It runs about a dozen catalog queries every 10 s as postgres_exporter (2 connections, 5 s timeout).

panels.title: Maintenance jobs
panels.description: One row per pg_cron job (0002_maintenance.sql), from monitoring.maintenance_status. Both run hourly, so Since last success over an hour means maintenance has stopped: partman makes no new partitions and drops none past retention, and the planner's statistics go stale. A job with no Last run has not run yet: the first runs at the next :00 or :30.

targets.rawSql: SELECT job_name AS "Job", schedule AS "Schedule", last_started_at AS "Last run", last_succeeded_at AS "Last success", extract(epoch FROM now() - last_succeeded_at) AS "Since last success", failed_runs_last_day AS "Failed (24 h)" FROM monitoring.maintenance_status ORDER BY job_name

panels.title: Partition coverage
panels.description: One row per partitioned table, from monitoring.partition_coverage. Premade should equal Premake: the months after this one that already have a partition. Past retention should be 0: maintenance drops a partition once it ended longer ago than Retention. Default rows should be 0: a row lands there only when no monthly partition covers its occurred_at. Since analyze over an hour means the hourly ANALYZE has stopped.

targets.rawSql: SELECT table_name AS "Table", premake AS "Premake", premade_partitions AS "Premade", retention AS "Retention", partitions_past_retention AS "Past retention", monthly_partitions AS "Partitions", oldest_partition_from AS "Oldest from", newest_partition_to AS "Newest to", default_partition_rows AS "Default rows", extract(epoch FROM now() - last_analyzed_at) AS "Since analyze", partitions_never_analyzed AS "Never analyzed" FROM monitoring.partition_coverage ORDER BY table_name

panels.title: Maintenance runs: last 20
panels.description: Every run of both pg_cron jobs, newest first, from monitoring.maintenance_runs. Read through a SECURITY DEFINER function, because pg_cron shows each role only its own jobs.

targets.rawSql: SELECT started_at AS "Started", job_name AS "Job", duration_seconds AS "Duration", status AS "Status", message AS "Message" FROM monitoring.maintenance_runs ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Table usage
panels.description: One row per table in txn_agg, a partitioned table summed over its partitions, from monitoring.table_usage. Scan counts are totals since the statistics were last reset, not for the selected range. Seq scans on transactions from the API mean a query is not using an index.

targets.rawSql: SELECT table_name AS "Table", table_bytes AS "Table size", index_bytes AS "Index size", live_rows AS "Live rows", dead_rows AS "Dead rows", sequential_scans AS "Seq scans", index_scans AS "Index scans" FROM monitoring.table_usage ORDER BY table_bytes + index_bytes DESC

panels.title: Index usage
panels.description: One row per index in txn_agg, an index on a partitioned table summed over its partitions, from monitoring.index_usage. idx_tx_user_read serves the API's list and summary, transactions_pkey its detail lookup. An index with no scans costs every insert and serves no read. Totals since the statistics were last reset.

targets.rawSql: SELECT table_name AS "Table", index_name AS "Index", scans AS "Scans", tuples_read AS "Tuples read", index_bytes AS "Size" FROM monitoring.index_usage ORDER BY index_bytes DESC

panels.title: Statements by role, with query text
panels.description: The 25 statement shapes with the most total time in txn_agg, from monitoring.statement_stats: one row per role and statement, parameters as $1, $2, …. Slowest statements above has the same numbers for the selected range, by queryid; this one has the query text. Mean plan is planning time per call. Totals since pg_stat_statements was last reset.

targets.rawSql: SELECT role_name AS "Role", calls AS "Calls", total_milliseconds AS "Total", mean_milliseconds AS "Mean", max_milliseconds AS "Max", mean_plan_milliseconds AS "Mean plan", rows_per_call AS "Rows/call", shared_blocks_hit AS "Blocks hit", shared_blocks_read AS "Blocks read", query AS "Query" FROM monitoring.statement_stats ORDER BY total_milliseconds DESC LIMIT 25
